text: The module code of a feature is its service code, so the 19 modules P1 to P10 and S1 to S9 are the 19 services of Arch v5 and the Ownership Map, one to one. The Service column is written '<code> <short name>' ('P1 rwb-source-data') and the Service epic 'RWB-SVC-<code>'. The module name stays as the workbook writes it and is not replaced by the service name.
why: The WP asks for a Service and a Service epic column on every feature and the source has neither; a rule is needed for all 378 rows that invents no value and does not rename a module. Architecture v5 states that recovery-core is split into 19 services, one per business module, which makes the code-to-service mapping a reading of the source rather than a new decision.

applied_in: Features columns O and P on 378 rows; By module columns H and I on 19 rows; Key sheet Column rows; Read me What changed note 1 and Counts
confirm: Business architect and the platform solution architect at the document review
impact: Two appended columns only; no module code, module name, feature ID, class, text, role, process, system, epic, release, story key or dependency changes

text: The single recovery schema of FEAT-RDF-01 and the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views of FEAT-RDF-25 are delivered as one schema per service in the same ACE database, with the built migration kept and 19 rwb_<name> schemas created. The v_ace_* view names stay as the source and Architecture v5 write them, and only rwb-source-data reads them.
why: The feature rows describe the built monolith position; the split is the D-RCV-60 change and is already ruled in R6 and DP-01. Keeping the text word for word and placing the split in the platform and per-service DB stories is the only reading that both preserves the rows and realises the target.

text: The ten interaction-ledger features stay listed in module P7 with the Service column at P7 rwb-decision, and their build ownership is split at story stage: the ledger write, the ledger store and the intake rule are P1 rwb-source-data work through its contract (DP-18), the timeline on the case and the interaction API are P3 rwb-case work, and the retention class is applied through P5 rwb-document's retention contract.
why: The workbook has one Module column and no owner column, so it cannot show a split; the module rule of ASM-B-BIZ-36-1 keeps the workbook consistent, and the Ownership Map ruling already settles who holds the ledger. Without this assumption the Service column would silently contradict the map on ten rows.

text: FEAT-RDF-20, FEAT-DRI-06 and FEAT-RPT-04 stay in the workbook word for word as live System features, are not built, and are recorded as retired-by-realignment at story stage: the local decision record plus the central ledger replaces the lake copy and rwb-reporting reads DecisionRecorded.
why: The source lists them as live and the workbook must keep its rows; D-RCV-60 retires their legacy story E1-014 with no new story, so the disposition has to be carried somewhere and the Change Register is where R6 puts it. Deleting or rewriting the rows would break the promise that every ID and number of the source is kept.

text: The seven features that name the Data lake and Power BI are delivered against rwb-reporting: each read is served by the rwb-reporting read model built from events, the extract is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-reporting, and no data lake and no Power BI connection is built. No row text changes.
why: DP-17 removes the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20 with it, and the target names rwb-reporting as the source of reports; the seven rows would otherwise name a system that does not exist in the target. Reading them against rwb-reporting keeps every measure and report the features describe.

text: No wave column is added to the workbook. The wave of a feature is read at story stage under R5.6 from its business epic through W-MAP, and a story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service wave keeps the W-MAP wave.
why: The WP asks for the Service and Service epic columns only, and the source has no wave attribute; adding one would put two rules of wave (service wave and W-MAP wave) into a single cell and invent a value the source does not carry. The Counts note states both so the reader is not left without the information.
